title: Teacher-written top-level model
subject: English Language
source: Written for english-language/y10 lesson 45 (Teacher-written top-level model (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 45: Self-assessment against the mark scheme and DIRT. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

passage.title: Teacher-written model for TGA (Section C, task c)
paras: The snow came in the night, quietly, as if it did not want to wake anyone. By morning the road had vanished. Where there had been tarmac, potholes and the grey scar of a patched-up trench, there was only white, smooth as a page nobody had written on.
Nothing moved. Then, far off, a single car crept round the bend, its tyres whispering, leaving two dark lines behind it like the first words of a sentence.

panels.title: Top-level features
points: An ending that echoes the opening

keywords.def: judging your own work against criteria
the one thing to do better next time
an example of a top-level piece

questions.q: Self-assess your timed piece: one AO4 level and one AO5 level, each with a reason.
questions.a: Levels with evidence from the piece and the ladder.

questions.q: Find one thing the model does that your piece does not.
questions.a: For example: a sustained image or a short sentence for emphasis.

questions.q: Core: DIRT in the portal response box. Redraft your weakest paragraph to reach the next level. Starter: paste the paragraph, then improve it.
questions.a: A redraft showing a clear AO4 or AO5 improvement.

questions.q: Extend: write your Section C target for Summer 1.
questions.a: A precise target, e.g. 'One sustained image in every piece.'

questions.q: Stretch: rewrite your opening sentence to be as striking as the model's.
What is the strongest feature of the model?
options: A sustained image that carries the whole piece
questions.a: C) A sustained image that carries the whole piece. The page image links opening and ending; length and adjectives are not the point.

questions.q: How confident are you with Section C now?
Answer the ponder in one sentence.
questions.a: Answers vary; most find weaknesses easier, so we use the ladder to see strengths too.
